hook.text: In 1637, one tulip bulb sold for the price of an Amsterdam mansion. Months later, tulips were worthless. Nobody saw it.

buildup.text: Bubbles form when prices reflect what the next buyer will pay, not underlying value.

discovery.text: Shiller showed that social contagion drives bubbles. Stories spread, excitement builds, and prices detach.

twist.text: Rational people can fuel irrational bubbles. If you believe others will keep buying, riding the bubble is individually.

climax.text: Bubbles end when the last buyer arrives. When no one is left to buy, the cascade reverses and prices collapse.

punchline.text: Every bubble has a last buyer. Don't be that person.

quiz.question: What drives speculative bubbles according to Shiller?
options: Perfectly rational calculation by all participants
